body.statement: There exist universal constants \(0<a_0\leq A_0<\infty\) such that, whenever \(T\geq2k_n\), \(a_0\min\{1,n^{-1}+c^2\}\leq R(n,T,c)\leq A_0\min\{1,n^{-1}+c^2\}\) and \(a_0\min\{1,n^{-1/2}+c\}\leq L(n,T,c)\leq A_0\min\{1,n^{-1/2}+c\}\). The upper estimator is the clipped natural sample mean, the interval adds the deterministic radius \(B(c)\) to a Hoeffding radius, and the lower bounds range over every measurable estimator and every possibly randomized honest connected interval.
body.justification: The theorem establishes a substantive non-oracle penalty in a solved regime and pins its exact shrinking-strength transition.
body.gap: KimKennedyNaimi2021 gives a special constant-propensity variance comparison, and MaZhuJiaoWainwright2022 gives a one-stage fixed-target oracle gap; neither proves this unrestricted sequential long-history result.
body.consumer: Many-visit incremental-intervention workflows obtain a rigorous warning that stable oracle weights need not imply uniform root-\(n\) estimation when histories are learned.
